lessons.title: What is a Return Value?
lessons.content: A function can return a value using 'return', like return x + y to give back a sum.

lessons.question: What does 'return' do in a function?

lessons.title: Creating Return Functions
lessons.content: Use 'def' and 'return', like def add(a, b): return a + b.

lessons.title: Write a function sum_nums(a, b) that returns a + b.
Using Return Values
lessons.content: Store the return value, like result = add(2, 3), to use it later.

lessons.question: What does def x(): return 5 give when called?

lessons.title: Returning Different Types
lessons.content: Return numbers, strings, or booleans, like return 'hello' or return True.

lessons.title: Write a function is_even(num) that returns True if num is even.
Early Returns
lessons.content: Use return to exit a function early, like if x < 0: return False.

lessons.question: Can a function return a string?

lessons.title: Return Power
lessons.content: Return values make functions flexible for calculations and decisions.

lessons.title: Return Master! 🎁
lessons.content: You’re returning values like a pro! Your functions are super useful!

lessons.title: What are Nested Loops?
lessons.content: A loop inside another loop, like a for loop inside a for loop.

lessons.title: Writing Nested Loops
lessons.content: Indent the inner loop, like for i in range(2): for j in range(2): print(i, j).

lessons.title: Print pairs from [1, 2] and ['a', 'b'].
How They Work
lessons.content: The inner loop runs completely for each iteration of the outer loop.

lessons.question: How many times does the inner loop run if outer loop runs 2 times?

lessons.title: Uses of Nested Loops
lessons.content: Great for combining lists or creating patterns.

lessons.title: Print a 2x2 grid of '*'.
Indentation
lessons.content: Inner loop code is indented under the outer loop.

lessons.instruction: Print i, j in nested loop.
lessons.starterCode:
for i in range(2):
    for j in range(2):

lessons.question: What does nested loop indentation show?

lessons.title: Nested Loop Power
lessons.content: Nested loops help process complex data combinations.

lessons.title: Nested Loop Ninja! 🔄
lessons.content: You’re mastering loops inside loops! Your code is tackling big tasks!

lessons.title: What is List Slicing?
lessons.content: Slicing gets a part of a list, like list[1:3] to get items 1 to 2.

lessons.title: Using Slices
lessons.content: Use [start:end], like nums[1:3] to get a sublist.

lessons.title: Slice Shortcuts
lessons.content: Use [:n] for start to n, or [n:] for n to end.

lessons.title: Negative Indices
lessons.content: Use negative indices, like [-1] for last item.

lessons.title: Step in Slicing
lessons.content: Use [start:end:step], like [::2] to get every second item.

lessons.title: Slicing Power
lessons.content: Slicing lets you work with parts of lists easily.

lessons.title: Slicing Star! ✂️
lessons.content: You’re cutting lists like a pro! Slicing makes your code precise!

lessons.title: What are List Methods?
lessons.content: Methods like .sort() or .pop() change or get info from lists.

lessons.title: Using Sort
lessons.content: Sorts in ascending order, like [3, 1].sort() makes [1, 3].

lessons.title: Pop Method
lessons.content: Pop removes and returns an item, like list.pop() for the last item.

lessons.title: Reverse Method
lessons.content: Reverse flips the list, like [1, 2].reverse() makes [2, 1].

lessons.title: Index Method
lessons.content: Find item’s index, like list.index('a') returns 0 if 'a' is first.

lessons.title: Method Power
lessons.content: List methods make lists dynamic and easy to manage.

lessons.title: List Method Guru! 📋
lessons.content: You’re transforming lists like a pro! Methods make your code powerful!

lessons.title: What are Dictionary Methods?
lessons.content: Methods like .keys() or .values() work with dictionary data.

lessons.title: Using Keys
lessons.content: Get all keys, like dict.keys() for {'a': 1} returns ['a'].

lessons.title: Values Method
lessons.content: Get all values, like dict.values() returns ['Mia', 10].

lessons.title: Items Method
lessons.content: Get key-value pairs, like dict.items() returns [('a', 1)].

lessons.title: Pop Method
lessons.content: Remove a key-value pair, like dict.pop('key') returns the value.

lessons.title: Dictionary Method Power
lessons.content: Methods make dictionaries flexible for data tasks.

lessons.title: Dictionary Method Pro! 📖
lessons.content: You’re mastering dictionary methods! Your code is super organized!

lessons.title: What is Splitting?
lessons.content: Split turns a string into a list, like 'a b'.split() makes ['a', 'b'].

lessons.title: Using Split
lessons.content: Split on spaces by default, or specify, like 'a,b'.split(',').

lessons.title: Split 'cat dog' into a list and print.
Custom Split
lessons.content: Split on any character, like 'x-y'.split('-') makes ['x', 'y'].

lessons.title: Saving Splits
lessons.content: Store the list, like words = text.split(), to use it.

lessons.title: Split Uses
lessons.content: Split is great for processing text into parts.

lessons.title: Split Power
lessons.content: Splitting makes text easy to work with in lists.

lessons.title: Split Specialist! 🔪
lessons.content: You’re breaking text into lists like a pro! Splitting is your superpower!

lessons.title: What is Joining?
lessons.content: Join combines a list into a string, like ','.join(['a', 'b']) makes 'a,b'.

lessons.title: Using Join
lessons.content: Choose a separator, like ' '.join(['hi', 'there']) makes 'hi there'.

lessons.title: Custom Join
lessons.content: Use any separator, like '-'.join(['x', 'y']) makes 'x-y'.

lessons.title: Saving Joins
lessons.content: Store the result, like text = ' '.join(list), to use it.

lessons.title: Join Uses
lessons.content: Join is great for formatting lists into text.

lessons.title: Join Power
lessons.content: Joining makes lists into clean, readable strings.

lessons.title: Join Jedi! 🧵
lessons.content: You’re stitching lists into strings like a pro! Joining is your craft!

lessons.title: What is Error Handling?
lessons.content: Use try/except to catch errors, like trying to convert bad input.

lessons.title: Writing Try/Except
lessons.content: Use try: code that might fail, except: code to handle the error.

lessons.title: Try converting 'abc' to int, print 'Error' if it fails.
Specific Errors
lessons.content: Catch specific errors, like except ValueError: for bad int conversions.

lessons.title: Why Handle Errors?
lessons.content: Prevents crashes and makes programs user-friendly.

lessons.title: Try dividing 10 by 0, print 'Cannot divide' if error.
Simple Handling
lessons.content: Keep try/except blocks small to focus on specific errors.

lessons.title: Error Handling Power
lessons.content: Error handling makes programs robust and reliable.

lessons.title: Error Handler! 🛡️
lessons.content: You’re catching errors like a pro! Your code is bulletproof!

lessons.title: What is Dictionary Looping?
lessons.content: Loop through keys, values, or pairs, like for k in dict:.

lessons.question: What can you loop through in a dictionary?

lessons.title: Looping Keys
lessons.content: Use for key in dict: to get keys, like for k in {'a': 1}: print(k).

lessons.title: Print keys of {'name': 'Mia', 'age': 10}.
Looping Values
lessons.content: Use dict.values(), like for v in dict.values(): print(v).

lessons.question: What does for v in {'a': 5}.values(): give?

lessons.title: Looping Items
lessons.content: Use dict.items() for key-value pairs, like for k, v in dict.items().

lessons.title: Print key-value pairs of {'color': 'blue'}.
When to Loop
lessons.content: Loop dictionaries to process or display their data.

lessons.question: What does for k, v in {'x': 1}.items(): give?

lessons.title: Dictionary Loop Power
lessons.content: Looping dictionaries makes data processing easy.

lessons.title: Dict Loop Dynamo! 🔄
lessons.content: You’re looping dictionaries like a pro! Your code is data-smart!

lessons.title: What is Key Sorting?
lessons.content: Sort lists with a key function, like sort(key=len) to sort by length.

lessons.title: Using Key
lessons.content: Pass a function, like ['cat', 'a'].sort(key=len) to sort by string length.

lessons.title: Reverse Sort
lessons.content: Use reverse=True, like sort(key=len, reverse=True) for descending.

lessons.title: Custom Key
lessons.content: Define your own key function, like def key_func(x): return x[0].

lessons.title: Sort ['red', 'blue'] by last letter.
lessons.expectedAnswer:
def last_letter(x):
    return x[-1]
colors = ['red', 'blue']
colors.sort(key=last_letter)
print(colors)

lessons.title: Key Uses
lessons.content: Key sorting is great for custom ordering.

lessons.question: Can you sort by a custom function?

lessons.title: Sort Key Power
lessons.content: Key sorting makes lists ordered in creative ways.

lessons.title: Sort Key Sorcerer! 🔠
lessons.content: You’re sorting with keys like a pro! Your lists are perfectly ordered!

lessons.title: What are Combined Conditionals?
lessons.content: Use and, or to combine conditions, like if x > 0 and x < 10:.

lessons.title: Using And
lessons.content: Both conditions must be true, like if age > 5 and age < 12:.

lessons.title: If x = 8, print 'OK' if x > 5 and x < 10.
Using Or
lessons.content: One condition must be true, like if x < 0 or x > 100:.

lessons.instruction: Use or for x < 1 or x > 5.

lessons.question: What does x > 1 or x < 0 return for x = 2?

lessons.title: Not Operator
lessons.content: Not reverses a condition, like if not x == 0:.

lessons.title: If x = 0, print 'Not zero' if x is not 0.
Complex Conditions
lessons.content: Combine multiple and/or, like if x > 0 and (y < 5 or z > 10):.

lessons.instruction: Use and for x > 0 and y < 2.
lessons.starterCode:
x = 1
y = 1
if x > 0  y < 2:
    print('Good')

lessons.question: What does not x == 1 return for x = 1?

lessons.title: Conditional Power
lessons.content: Combining conditions makes decisions precise.

lessons.title: Conditional Combiner! ✅
lessons.content: You’re mixing conditions like a pro! Your code is super smart!

lessons.title: What are Break and Continue?
lessons.content: Break stops a loop, continue skips to the next iteration.

lessons.title: Using Break
lessons.content: Use break to exit, like if x == 5: break to stop at 5.

lessons.title: Stop loop at 3 in range(5).
Using Continue
lessons.content: Skip rest of loop, like if x % 2 == 0: continue to skip evens.

lessons.title: When to Use
lessons.content: Break for early exit, continue for skipping specific cases.

lessons.title: Print odd numbers from [1, 2, 3, 4] using continue.
Loop Control
lessons.content: Break and continue give you control over loop flow.

lessons.title: Loop Control Power
lessons.content: Break and continue make loops flexible and efficient.

lessons.title: Loop Controller! 🎮
lessons.content: You’re controlling loops like a pro! Break and continue are your tools!

lessons.title: What are Tuples?
lessons.content: Tuples are like lists but unchangeable, like (1, 2).

lessons.title: Creating Tuples
lessons.content: Use (), like coords = (3, 4) to store fixed data.

lessons.title: Accessing Items
lessons.content: Use index, like tuple[0] to get first item.

lessons.title: Tuple Uses
lessons.content: Tuples are great for fixed data, like coordinates or settings.

lessons.title: Tuple Length
lessons.content: Use len(), like len((1, 2)) returns 2.

lessons.title: Tuple Power
lessons.content: Tuples keep data safe and simple for fixed collections.

lessons.title: Tuple Titan! 📍
lessons.content: You’re using tuples like a pro! Your code is rock-solid!

lessons.title: What is a List?
lessons.content: A list is a collection of items in Python, defined using square brackets [].

lessons.question: Which of these is a valid list?

lessons.title: Accessing List Items
lessons.content: Use an index to access a list item: my_list[0] gets the first item.

lessons.title: Modifying Lists
lessons.content: You can add items with append() or change items by assigning to an index.

lessons.title: Looping Through Lists
lessons.content: Use a for loop to go through items: for x in my_list: print(x)

lessons.title: Print each item in the list.
List Length
lessons.content: Use len(my_list) to get the number of items in the list.

lessons.instruction: Get the length of the list.

lessons.title: List Power
lessons.content: Lists help you store and organize lots of data in Python.

lessons.title: List Master! 📝
lessons.content: You're working with lists like a Python pro!
